fact: Mali's specialised cybercrime tribunal sentenced journalist Abdrahamane Keita, publication director of Le Temoin, to two years in prison and 1 million CFA francs damages for a remark about Kidal on a TV programme on 4 June 2026, on charges of regionalist remarks, undermining the State's credit and national unity, and spreading false information through an information system; he had been detained since June and the defence intends to appeal.

Journalist Abdrahamane Keita of Le Temoin was detained on 9 June 2026 over comments on the security situation in northern Mali made on a live media programme, and charged with undermining national unity and the credibility of the state and disseminating false information, says IPI.

Journalist Chahana Takiou, editor of 22 Septembre, was sentenced on 3 August 2026 to 12 months in prison, six suspended, and fined, for undermining the credibility of the state; he had been arrested in June 2026 by the National Cybercrime Unit after criticising its use against journalists at the Pan-African Media Forum in Bamako, says IPI.

Radio and television commentator Mohamed Youssouf Bathily (Ras Bath) was arrested in March 2023 after public comments about the death in custody of a former prime minister and has been in detention since, says IPI.

The trial of Mohamed Youssouf Bathily (Ras Bath) began on 10 August 2026 on charges of criminal association and undermining the credibility of the state through information and communication technologies, says IPI.

The national cybercrime unit sentenced journalist Chahana Takiou, founder-publisher of 22 septembre, to 12 months in prison with 6 suspended for undermining the State's credit through the judicial institution, after he said at the Pan-African Media Forum in June 2026 that journalists should be tried under the press-offence law rather than the cybercrime law.
